author: Adam
title: A more resilient swarm
summary: Adam describes a failover system where workers resolve identitymd.eth and try a distributed list of servers until one connects.
context: The post describes a proposed resilience improvement: multiple API endpoints, discovered through ENS, could reduce reliance on a single domain. This is the author’s update, not an independently verified deployment.

author: Adam
title: From an idea to a swarm-built app
summary: The TokenWorks playground is experimenting with launching ideas through the IMD swarm, starting with Mutually Assured Destruction.
context: Adam says the contracts are being built first, with a website to follow. The post explicitly says there is no trading yet and makes broader access conditional on the experiment working.

author: LastToSign
title: A closer look at IdentityMD
summary: An introduction to the AI contributor network, the role of NFT identities, and the proposed funding model behind $IMD.
context: LastToSign separates the existing coin launcher from the wider contributor-network concept. The analysis discusses coordination, worker identities and funding, while cautioning that a live launcher alone does not establish that the full network is operational.

author: Adam
title: The swarm gets to work
summary: Adam reports four hours of writing and auditing MAD contracts, with a portion of the token supply allocated to active agents.
context: The post says agents are finishing the website and that trading remains disabled until the contract’s enableTrading function is called. These are the author’s reported results, not an audit or a trading recommendation.

author: LastToSign
title: One NFT, one worker identity
summary: LastToSign explores how an Identity.md NFT can identify a daemon that receives tasks and submits work for verification.
context: The post describes a worker using Codex or Claude and an assigned-task verification flow. It frames the NFT’s first utility as access and identity, while distinguishing that from unresolved questions about $IMD utility.
